title: Vinted Return Swap Scam: Buyer Returned a Different Item — What to Do
intro: If a Vinted buyer returns a completely different item than the one you sent, dispute the return in the order chat immediately, upload your evidence (packing photos, serial numbers, tags, parcel weight), and if Vinted still refunds them, escalate with a formal complaint to Vinted's legal team (legal@vinted.com) and a letter before action. Sellers have recovered their money by refusing to let the case close — the swap only works when the seller gives up.
meta_description: The Vinted return swap scam explained: buyers claim the wrong item was sent, then return a completely different item and keep yours. How to spot it, dispute it, and win.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Never miss a scam warning or a deal again — get instant alerts for the items you want on Vinted

body.heading: What the return swap scam actually is
paragraphs: The return swap scam — also called the "switcheroo" — is one of the most reported seller complaints on Vinted right now. It works in four steps. A buyer purchases your item, receives it, then opens an issue claiming you sent the wrong item, that it's fake, or that it arrived damaged. Vinted authorises a return. The buyer sends back a completely different item — their own old, worn, broken, or cheap counterfeit version — and keeps the one you sent. You get back junk, and the buyer gets your item plus a refund.

Recent threads on r/vinted and r/vintedUK describe this exact pattern again and again: a seller ships a Gymshark compression shirt and the buyer's "wrong item" photo shows a different design with a different size tag; a seller's brand-new sneakers come back as a worn pair with the original box stuffing swapped in; a seller's designer bag is returned as a battered version with paint stains and missing accessories; a console comes back water-damaged. Long-time sellers in the comments sum it up bluntly: "this is happening all the time now on vinted."

body.heading: How the scam plays out, step by step
paragraphs: The pattern is consistent across the threads. The buyer usually targets a higher-value item and often has very few reviews — one reported seller noted a buyer with just two positive reviews buying a designer bag outright, no haggling, asking lots of questions first. Once the parcel arrives, the claim appears quickly: "wrong item sent" with a photo of something that was never in your listing. If the buyer is smarter, they claim the item is counterfeit or "damaged in transit due to bad packaging".

Vinted then authorises a return. This is the critical moment: the return process is designed around the assumption that the buyer sends back the item they received, and Vinted does not verify the return contents before releasing the refund. Sellers describe being told to accept the return and open a dispute only after it arrives. When the parcel lands, it's the wrong item — and Vinted's support often responds with copy-paste replies, delays, or a decision in the buyer's favour.

There's another reason this keeps working: Vinted doesn't let you leave a review on cancelled or refunded transactions, so serial scammers keep clean profiles and the warning signs never show up in their feedback.

body.heading: What to do the moment the return arrives
paragraphs: Treat the returned parcel like a crime scene. Film one continuous, unedited video: the parcel label and tracking number, the sealed package, you opening it, and the item inside. Do not stop and restart the recording. Then photograph the returned item from every angle, including the tags, labels, and any serial number or date code.

Build a side-by-side comparison against what you sent: your listing photos, your pre-dispatch photos, serial number or tag details, accessories included, and condition. If the returned parcel weighs noticeably less or more than the one you shipped, note that too — commenters point out that a cheap counterfeit almost never weighs the same as the genuine item, and parcel weight records can support your case.

Message Vinted in the same order case, factually and without emotion: the returned item is not the item you sent; you have pre-dispatch evidence; you have a continuous unboxing video; you suspect return-swap fraud; you want the case escalated to a senior fraud team and you do not want it closed until the evidence is reviewed. Ask for a final written response explaining the decision. One seller who sold a designer bag only got the case taken seriously after sending a letter before action and stating they would file at small claims — the case was then escalated, Vinted admitted mistakes, and the seller was paid.

body.heading: Evidence that actually wins these cases
paragraphs: Sellers who win have one thing in common: proof of exactly what they sent. The evidence that repeatedly works:

Photos of the item before packing that include the serial number, size tag, date code, or any unique marking. Videos can be useful but Vinted's dispute form accepts photos, so make sure your photos stand alone.

A discreet identifier only you know about — several sellers recommend a small permanent-marker dot on the underside of an insole or inside a seam, photographed before shipping. If the returned item lacks your mark, that's hard to argue with.
The courier drop-off receipt and any recorded parcel weight at the time you shipped.
Your full listing photos, saved before the sale, so the buyer's "wrong item" photo can be compared side by side.

All message screenshots, especially anything where the buyer contradicts themselves — in one case the buyer first said the item "doesn't fit my son" and only later claimed it was the wrong item entirely.

body.heading: How to protect your next sale
paragraphs: Prevention beats any dispute. The habits sellers describe after getting burned:

Check the buyer before accepting a high-value offer — account age, review count, and whether they've ever sold anything. New accounts with one or two reviews buying expensive items instantly are the classic setup.
Photograph every item you ship with its serial number or tag visible, and take a picture of the packed parcel. Do it for cheap items too; it takes thirty seconds.

For genuinely valuable items, consider Vinted's optional item verification where it's offered — sellers note the buyer chooses whether to pay for it, and some now refuse to sell high-value items unless the buyer opts in. It shifts the authentication burden away from you.

Be extra careful with items that are easy to swap or fake — sneakers, designer bags, and consoles are the ones that keep appearing in these threads. If you can't afford to lose it, don't ship it on Vinted without verification.

body.heading: If Vinted refunds the buyer anyway: escalation routes
paragraphs: Don't accept the loss as final. The sellers who recovered money all escalated beyond the in-app chat:
1. Reopen the case or file a formal complaint demanding a final written response that confirms whether your evidence was reviewed.
2. Email Vinted's legal team — legal@vinted.com is listed on Vinted's official dispute-resolution page (vinted.com/help/1253). State the facts, attach your evidence, and give a deadline.
3. Report the buyer for fraud or theft to your local police and get a crime reference number — it strengthens every later escalation.
4. Send a letter before action, then file at small claims if they don't resolve it. Sellers report Vinted often settles once a real claim is on the table rather than defend it.
The pattern from every successful case is the same: the system is designed to wear you down, and it only pays out to sellers who refuse to stop pushing.

faq.question: Is the return swap scam common on Vinted?
faq.answer: Yes. It's one of the most frequently reported seller scams on r/vinted and r/vintedUK, with new threads appearing regularly — the same week a seller reported a £750 designer bag swap, others described swapped sneakers, consoles, and clothing. Long-time sellers say they now refuse to sell anything over a small amount on Vinted without extra protection.

faq.question: Can I win a dispute if the buyer returns a different item?
faq.answer: Yes, sellers do win — but usually only after escalating. The winning cases all had pre-dispatch photos with serial numbers or unique marks, a continuous unboxing video of the return, and a formal escalation (legal email, letter before action, or police report). Vinted often sides with the buyer initially; the cases that get reversed are the ones where the seller refuses to let it drop.

faq.question: Does Vinted check the returned item before refunding the buyer?
faq.answer: In the cases sellers describe, the refund is released as part of the return process and the wrong item is only discovered when it arrives. That's exactly why you must document the return the moment it lands and dispute it in the same order case before the case closes.

faq.question: Should I record myself packing Vinted orders?
faq.answer: It's cheap insurance and the standard advice in every scam thread. But note that Vinted's dispute form accepts photos, not videos — so make sure your photos show the serial number, tag, or a discreet mark you placed on the item. Keep the video as backup and mention it when you escalate.

faq.question: What if the buyer has few reviews — is that a red flag?
faq.answer: Often, yes. In the reported swap cases the buyers frequently had very few reviews and bought high-value items quickly or with a lot of probing questions. A brand-new account buying an expensive item outright is worth extra scrutiny — check their reviews, their listings, and consider requiring Vinted's item verification for the sale.

faq.question: Can I get the scammer banned from Vinted?
faq.answer: You can report them to Vinted's Trust & Safety team, and you should. But sellers report that accounts involved in swap scams have stayed active even after detailed reports, so don't rely on a ban as your remedy — pursue the refund through the escalation route above first.
